questions.question: Describe how sieving, settling and decanting are used to clean stream water.
questions.expected_answer: Pour the water through a clean cloth or sieve to remove leaves, twigs and grit. Leave it to stand so that sand and mud settle to the bottom as sediment. Then carefully pour the clearer water off the top into a clean container, leaving the sediment behind, which is decanting.

questions.question: How can you make a simple water filter, and why is filtered water not yet safe to drink?
questions.expected_answer: Cut the bottom off a plastic bottle, cover the neck with cloth, turn it upside down and fill it with cotton wool, charcoal, fine sand, coarse sand and gravel. Pour the water through and collect the clear water that drips out. It is not yet safe because filtering does not remove all germs, which are too small to see, or dissolved substances.

questions.question: Describe two ways to kill germs in water and how to store clean water.
questions.expected_answer: Boil the water at a rolling boil for at least one minute, then let it cool with a lid on. Or an adult adds one teaspoon of plain household bleach to 25 litres of water, stirs and waits at least two hours; purification tablets also work. Store the water in a clean container with a lid and pour it out instead of dipping hands in.
